key_insight: FAME introduces a failure-aware mixture-of-experts that performs message-level log anomaly detection, letting the model disambiguate event templates that occur in both normal and faulty contexts and handle heterogeneous failure modes in large-scale systems.
problem_solved: Most log anomaly detectors operate at session/window granularity and force operators to sift through many routine lines; this work pinpoints the exact anomalous message line within logs, reducing noise and accelerating triage.
method: Message-level modeling: operate directly on individual log lines (templates + context) instead of coarse sessions or windows.
Mixture-of-Experts architecture: allocate specialized experts to capture diverse failure patterns and subsystem heterogeneity.
Failure-aware routing/loss: bias gating and training signals toward separating normal vs. failure usages of the same template, enabling accurate localization of anomalies at line level.
impact: Finer-grained alerts reduce false positives and triage time for SREs/engineers, improving operational observability and enabling faster root-cause identification in production environments.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: MoE backbone with gating network and failure-aware loss, showing routing of ambiguous templates to different experts.
Before vs After comparison: session/window-level alert (many lines flagged) vs message-level highlight (single anomalous line highlighted).
Example log snippet: real log lines with color-coded anomaly scores and the selected expert for each anomalous line.
Metric sketch: conceptual chart showing reduced operator inspection time / false positive rate (no numeric claims required).
paper_title: FAME: Failure-Aware Mixture-of-Experts for Message-Level Log Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Huanchi Wang, Zihang Huang, Yifang Tian, Kristina Dzeparoska, Hans-Arno Jacobsen
